_readme: A worked example, not part of the kit's rubric. This is what an acceptance checklist looks like when it is written from a real brief — here a desk-and-parking booking prototype whose spec named a ten-step demo scenario. Copy the shape, not the content: your event's checklist comes from your event's brief. See docs/acceptance-checklist.template.json for how to write one.
event: Example — a two-day prototype event, desk and parking booking brief
_note_on_the_last_two: Every step below is something a facilitator can watch happen and be sure about. The brief also asked for multi-office support and a scalable architecture; neither is on this list, because neither can be observed in a demo. Those belong in the proposal a jury reads, not in a checklist someone scores live.

acceptance.label: An administrator creates or enables one desk and one parking space
An employee books both resources for the same working day
A second employee is prevented from booking the same desk for that day
The first employee checks in for the desk before the release deadline, by any method the team implemented
The team can move time past the release deadline on demand, rather than waiting for it
The checked-in desk booking survives, and the un-checked-in parking booking is released
The second employee can then book the released parking space
An administrator can see the booking, check-in and release history for that day
An administrator changes a rule or a resource status and the change is immediately in effect
The setup and run instructions get the prototype running on a machine that has never seen it
